chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Waddad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt owed to him by his wife, and she frees him from it during her illness. He said: 'Rather, she should gift it to him, and her gift to him is valid, and that is counted from her one-third, if she left anything.'
16 - From him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Nuh, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Razi, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man dies and bequeaths all his wealth in the channels of charity, and more than one-third. Is that valid for him, and what should the executor do? He wrote back: 'His bequest is valid as long as it does not exceed one-third.'
17 - As for what was narrated - Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdus, said:

A man bequeathed his estate, goods and otherwise, to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him). I wrote to him: 'I am your ransom, a man bequeathed to me all that he left for you, and he left two daughters of his sister. What is your opinion in this?' He wrote to me (peace be upon him): 'Sell what he left and send it to me.'
So I sold it and sent it to him, and he wrote to me: 'It has arrived.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Zur'ar died and bequeathed to my brother Ahmad, and he left a house. He had bequeathed that all his estate be sold and its price sent to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

So we sold it, and a son of his sister and a cousin of his contested it. We settled their matter with three dinars. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan wrote to him and handed over the matter in my presence to Ayub ibn Nuh.

And he informed him that it was all that he left, and his cousin and his sister's son contested, so we settled their matter with three dinars. He wrote: 'That has arrived,' and he prayed mercy for the deceased.

And I read the reply. Ali said: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Halabi died and left two hundred dirhams. He bequeathed to his wife something of her dowry and otherwise, and bequeathed the remainder to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).
Ahmad ibn al-Hasan handed them over to Ayub in my presence and wrote to him a letter. The reply came confirming receipt, and he prayed for the deceased.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The first thing we say is that when the reports come from them (peace be upon him) that they performed an action that contradicts what is established in the Sharia of Islam, it should be ruled that they are invalid or carried on a meaning in general that matches the sound reports, even if we do not know it in detail.

How much more so since we have mentioned from them (peace be upon him) in what preceded that they would reject from the bequests that which exceeded one-third and would not take more than it. This is the report of 'Amr ibn Sa'id in the story of Rumayy ibn 'Umar with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and the report of al-Husayn ibn Malik with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

And since we have mentioned that, it is necessary to reconcile these reports with them, on the basis that it is not impossible that this is a ruling specific to them (peace be upon him), that whoever bequeathed to them all the wealth or most of it, it was valid for them to take it, even if they had left it, that would be from their generosity, as we have presented.

And it is possible that the heirs who were for these people were differing from them in belief, so it was valid for them to prevent them from that, and it was permissible for them to dispose of all that was bequeathed to them.

And that the last report is specific, in which it is not mentioned that the one who bequeathed to him the wealth had an heir. And if that was not in it, it is possible that they only validated it because he had no heir, as we have presented in what preceded.

And Allah knows best what is correct in that, and they (peace be upon him) are more perceptive of what they did. So their actions are a Sharia for us, and it is obligatory upon us to submit to them without seeking to explain them, even though we have discussed them in a manner of approximation and clarification, on the basis that there is no contradiction between their statements and their actions in any state.
ai.seo_question: Can an Imam accept more than one-third of an estate in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights a jurisprudential nuance where the Imams accepted entire estates despite the general prohibition against bequeathing more than one-third, suggesting this was either a specific privilege (khass) for the Imams or due to the absence of competing heirs. This reconciles apparent contradictions in the hadith literature by distinguishing between the standard legal limit for general heirs and the unique authority of the Imams to accept full bequests as a form of divine right or discretionary gift.
